metadata.name: Immune Signaling Pathways
metadata.description: Curated immune-relevant signaling pathways with component interactions, based on KEGG and Reactome pathway databases

pathways.description: The JAK-STAT signaling pathway transduces signals from cytokines and growth factors through receptor-associated Janus kinases (JAKs) to signal transducers and activators of transcription (STATs). Upon ligand binding, JAKs phosphorylate STATs, which dimerize, translocate to the nucleus, and activate target gene transcription. This pathway is central to immune cell differentiation, proliferation, and inflammatory responses.

pathways.description: The NF-kappaB signaling pathway is a master regulator of innate and adaptive immunity, inflammation, and cell survival. The canonical pathway activates RELA/p50 dimers through IKK complex-mediated degradation of IkB-alpha, while the non-canonical pathway processes p100 to p52 via NIK and IKK-alpha. NF-kappaB drives expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, adhesion molecules, and anti-apoptotic genes.

pathways.description: Tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling mediates diverse cellular responses including inflammation, apoptosis, necroptosis, and cell survival. TNF binds TNFR1 (ubiquitous) or TNFR2 (immune cells), triggering recruitment of adaptor proteins to form distinct signaling complexes: Complex I activates NF-kappaB and MAPK pathways promoting survival, while Complex II (with FADD and caspase-8) or the necrosome (RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL) drive apoptosis or necroptosis respectively.

pathways.description: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pattern recognition receptors that detect pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). Signaling proceeds via MyD88-dependent (all TLRs except TLR3) and TRIF-dependent (TLR3 and TLR4) arms. MyD88-dependent signaling activates NF-kappaB and MAPK cascades driving pro-inflammatory cytokine production, while TRIF-dependent signaling activates IRF3/IRF7 inducing type I interferons.

pathways.description: T cell receptor (TCR) signaling is initiated when the TCR/CD3 complex recognizes peptide-MHC on antigen-presenting cells. Src family kinases LCK and FYN phosphorylate CD3 ITAMs, recruiting and activating ZAP70. ZAP70 phosphorylates the scaffold protein LAT and SLP-76, nucleating a signalosome that activates PLCgamma1, RAS-MAPK, and PI3K-AKT pathways. Downstream transcription factors NFAT, AP-1, and NF-kappaB cooperatively drive IL-2 expression and T cell activation.

pathways.description: B cell receptor (BCR) signaling is initiated when membrane immunoglobulin binds antigen, causing receptor clustering and phosphorylation of Igalpha/Igbeta ITAMs by LYN kinase. SYK is recruited to phosphorylated ITAMs and activates BLNK scaffold protein, which nucleates a signalosome containing BTK and PLCgamma2. Downstream pathways activate NF-kappaB, NFAT, and MAPK cascades driving B cell activation, proliferation, and differentiation into antibody-secreting cells.

pathways.description: The IL-17 signaling pathway mediates mucosal host defense and is pathogenic in numerous autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. IL-17A and IL-17F signal through heterodimeric IL-17RA/IL-17RC receptors, recruiting the adaptor ACT1 (TRAF3IP2). ACT1 engages TRAF6 to activate NF-kappaB and MAPK cascades, and also stabilizes mRNA of pro-inflammatory mediators through ACT1-TRAF2-SF2 complex. Downstream effectors include C/EBP transcription factors driving chemokine and antimicrobial peptide expression.

pathways.description: Th17 cell differentiation is driven by the combination of TGF-beta and IL-6, which activate STAT3 and induce the master transcription factor RORgamma-t (RORC). IL-23 is critical for stabilization and maintenance of the Th17 phenotype. IL-21 provides autocrine amplification. Th17 cells produce IL-17A, IL-17F, IL-22, and GM-CSF, playing essential roles in mucosal immunity and autoimmune pathology. The balance between Th17 and regulatory T cells is modulated by metabolic and epigenetic programs.

pathways.description: Th1 and Th2 cell differentiation represent two classical CD4+ T helper lineages with opposing immune functions. Th1 cells are driven by IL-12 and IFN-gamma via STAT4 and STAT1, inducing the master transcription factor T-bet (TBX21), which promotes IFN-gamma production for cell-mediated immunity. Th2 cells are driven by IL-4 via STAT6, inducing GATA3, which promotes IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13 production for humoral immunity and anti-helminth responses. Reciprocal antagonism between T-bet and GATA3 enforces lineage commitment.

pathways.description: Type I diabetes mellitus (T1D) is an autoimmune disease resulting from selective destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic beta cells by autoreactive CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes and CD4+ T helper cells. Key autoantigens include insulin (INS), glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD65), islet antigen-2 (IA-2), and zinc transporter 8 (ZnT8). Pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF, IL-1beta, and IFN-gamma synergistically induce beta cell apoptosis via Fas/FasL, perforin/granzyme, and ER stress pathways.

pathways.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a prototypic systemic autoimmune disease characterized by loss of tolerance to nuclear autoantigens, production of pathogenic autoantibodies (anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, anti-RNP), immune complex deposition, and complement activation. Defective clearance of apoptotic cells releases nuclear antigens that activate plasmacytoid dendritic cells via TLR7/TLR9, driving type I interferon production. The interferon signature amplifies autoimmune responses through enhanced antigen presentation and B cell activation.

pathways.description: The complement system is a proteolytic cascade of over 30 serum and membrane proteins that provides immediate defense against pathogens and bridges innate and adaptive immunity. Three activation pathways converge on C3 convertase: the classical pathway (C1q binding immune complexes), the lectin pathway (MBL/ficolins binding carbohydrates), and the alternative pathway (spontaneous C3 hydrolysis). Terminal pathway assembly of C5b-C9 forms the membrane attack complex (MAC). Complement also generates anaphylatoxins C3a and C5a, opsonins C3b and iC3b, and regulates immune complex clearance.
